research_question: Can fully coupled, finite-core closed vorticity lines retain an incoming excitation energy for a preregistered long late interval without dissipative terms, imposed velocity matching or selected angular symmetry?
objective: Negative-control-first screening of mutual vortex-ring dynamics. Report resolved energy redistribution and distinguish it from genuine trapping, 3D Euler closure, and photon absorption.
null_hypothesis: H0: observed receiver self-energy response does not establish persistent localized excess energy over four interaction time scales with scale-refined convergence; an unresolved run cannot reject H0.
alternative_hypothesis: H1: a fully coupled, well-resolved ring pair exhibits long-lived localized incoming-excitation energy above the preregistered null, across fixed physical times, insensitive to sampling and angular mode selection.
assumptions: Incompressible, inviscid constant density, no reconnection
Finite-width line-centered Rosenhead-Moore regularization is a model closure, not full 3D Euler
Both closed rings are fully back-reacting by the same Biot-Savart kernel
No artificial damping, velocity matching, wall, preferred azimuthal m, or forcing
Long-term capture requires full surface flux and material-volume diagnostics not available in v0.1.0

observables.definition: Total H_a and self/cross contributions versus time
Receiver H_RR drift proxy, NOT physical captured energy
True late retention fraction is unmeasured in v0.1.0

steps.operation: Verify frozen protocol and imported reference checksums
Construct two independent coaxial closed line samples without imposing mode m=5
Integrate both moving rings with explicit RK4 and the same finite-core regularized kernel; fixed absolute final time
Measure H_a, H_RR, H_LL, H_RL and energy conservation at each snapshot
Test far-separated mutual coupling as null
Probe temporal and spatial refinement separately at same final time
Reserve long-window retention criterion; do not infer from H_RR
Hold-out and native/third-party parity are not available and must not produce positive claims

falsification_criteria.criterion: If any energy drift exceeds registered 0.02 in normalized control or non-finite values occur, numerical gate G2 FAIL (invalid physics inference).
If a qualified full-field late local-energy measurement shows f_ret <0.5 in held-out cases, claim of persistent capture fails within tested regime.
If source-hash parity fails, reject source qualification and block downstream claim.

edge_cases: Cross-linking at near-core contact halts; no silent reconnection
A simple leapfrog exchange is not lasting capture
Finite-core smoothing changes dynamics; no convergence claims without core-resolution ladder
Line energy partition is not physical control-volume energy
predictions: Regularized ring self-motion and mutual effects observable for nearby coaxial rings
Cross energy decreases with sufficiently large separation
A true captured mode would require sustained localized excess energy after incoming wavepacket encounter; untested here
